claims.quote: Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail;
claims.summary: Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail.

claims.quote: This section sets forth special rules applicable to the offset of Federal benefit payments payable to an individual under the Social Security Act (other than Supplemental Security Income (SSI) payments), part B of the Black Lung Benefits Act, or any law administered by the Railroad Retirement Board (other than payments that such Board determines to be tier 2 benefits) to collect delinquent nontax debt owed to the United States.
claims.summary: This section sets forth special rules applicable to the offset of Federal benefit payments payable to an individual under the Social Security Act (other than Supplemental Security Income (SSI) payments), part B of the Black Lung Benefits Act, or any law administered by the Railroad Retirement Board (other than payments that such Board determines to be tier 2 benefits) to collect delinquent nontax debt owed to the United States.

claims.quote: Benefit payments “due to” an individual, “payable to” an individual, and/or benefit payments “received by” an individual, refer to those benefit payments expected to be paid to an individual before any amounts are offset to satisfy the payee's delinquent debt owed to the United States.
claims.summary: Benefit payments “due to” an individual, “payable to” an individual, and/or benefit payments “received by” an individual, refer to those benefit payments expected to be paid to an individual before any amounts are offset to satisfy the payee's delinquent debt owed to the United States.

claims.quote: The Bureau of the Fiscal Service (Fiscal Service), the Social Security Administration, the Railroad Retirement Board, and other payment agencies are not liable for the amount offset from an individual's benefit payment on the basis that the underlying obligation, represented by the payment before the offset was taken, was not satisfied.
claims.summary: The Bureau of the Fiscal Service (Fiscal Service), the Social Security Administration, the Railroad Retirement Board, and other payment agencies are not liable for the amount offset from an individual's benefit payment on the basis that the underlying obligation, represented by the payment before the offset was taken, was not satisfied.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials shall offset payments to satisfy, in whole or in part, debts owed by the payee.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must offset payments to satisfy debts owed by the payee.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials shall compare payment records with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must compare payment records with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: When a match occurs and all other requirements for offset have been met, the disbursing official shall offset the payment to satisfy, in whole or in part, the debt.
claims.summary: When a match occurs and all other requirements for offset have been met, the disbursing official must offset the payment to satisfy, in whole or in part, the debt.

claims.quote: Covered benefit payments... are among the types of payments which may be offset to collect debts owed to the United States.
claims.summary: Covered benefit payments may be offset to collect debts owed to the United States.

claims.quote: Offsets of covered benefit payments will occur only if the name and taxpayer identifying number of the person who is entitled to the benefit of all or a part of the payment matches the name and taxpayer identifying number of the debtor.
claims.summary: Offsets of covered benefit payments will occur only if the name and taxpayer identifying number of the person who is entitled to the benefit of all or a part of the payment matches the name and taxpayer identifying number of the debtor.

claims.quote: Creditor agencies must notify Fiscal Service of all past-due, legally enforceable debt delinquent for more than 120 days for purposes of collection by administrative offset.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must notify Fiscal Service of all past-due, legally enforceable debt delinquent for more than 120 days for purposes of collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: Prior to such notification, creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that the creditor agency has provided the debtor with notice and an opportunity for a review in accordance with the provisions of 31 U.S.C. 3716(a) and other applicable law.
claims.summary: Prior to such notification, creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that the creditor agency has provided the debtor with notice and an opportunity for a review in accordance with the provisions of 31 U.S.C. 3716(a) and other applicable law.

claims.quote: The amount offset from a monthly covered benefit payment shall be the lesser of: (i) The amount of the debt, including any interest, penalties and administrative costs; (ii) An amount equal to 15% of the monthly covered benefit payment; or (iii) The amount, if any, by which the monthly covered benefit payment exceeds $750.
claims.summary: The amount offset from a monthly covered benefit payment shall be the lesser of: (i) The amount of the debt, including any interest, penalties and administrative costs; (ii) An amount equal to 15% of the monthly covered benefit payment; or (iii) The amount, if any, by which the monthly covered benefit payment exceeds $750.

claims.quote: A debtor shall not receive a refund of any amounts offset if the debtor's monthly covered benefit payments are reduced, suspended, terminated, or otherwise not received for a period of 12 months.
claims.summary: A debtor shall not receive a refund of any amounts offset if the debtor's monthly covered benefit payments are reduced, suspended, terminated, or otherwise not received for a period of 12 months.

claims.quote: Before offsetting a covered benefit payment, the disbursing official will notify the payee in writing of the date offset will commence. The notice shall inform the payee of the type of payment that will be offset; the identity of the creditor agency which requested the offset; and a contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.summary: Before offsetting a covered benefit payment, the disbursing official will notify the payee in writing of the date offset will commence. The notice shall inform the payee of the type of payment that will be offset; the identity of the creditor agency which requested the offset; and a contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.

claims.quote: The disbursing official conducting the offset will notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset to satisfy, in whole or in part, a delinquent debt owed to the United States. The notice shall inform the payee of the type and amount of the payment that was offset; the identity of the creditor agency which requested the offset; and a contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.summary: The disbursing official conducting the offset will notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset to satisfy, in whole or in part, a delinquent debt owed to the United States. The notice shall inform the payee of the type and amount of the payment that was offset; the identity of the creditor agency which requested the offset; and a contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.

claims.quote: A fee which Fiscal Service has determined to be sufficient to cover the full cost of the offset procedure, shall be deducted from each offset amount. Creditor agencies may add this fee to the debt if not otherwise prohibited by law.
claims.summary: A fee which Fiscal Service has determined to be sufficient to cover the full cost of the offset procedure, shall be deducted from each offset amount. Creditor agencies may add this fee to the debt if not otherwise prohibited by law.

claims.quote: Offset occurs when the Federal government withholds part or all of a debtor's Federal payment to satisfy the debtor's delinquent debt owed to the government.
claims.summary: The Federal government must withhold part or all of a debtor's Federal payment to satisfy the debtor's delinquent debt owed to the government.

claims.quote: The receipt of collections pursuant to this section does not preclude a Federal agency from pursuing other debt collection remedies in conjunction with centralized offset.
claims.summary: A Federal agency must not preclude the receipt of collections pursuant to this section from pursuing other debt collection remedies in conjunction with centralized offset.

claims.quote: Nothing in this section precludes an agency from pursuing all available debt collection remedies simultaneously, provided that collections do not exceed the amount of the debt, including any interest, penalties, and administrative costs.
claims.summary: An agency must not preclude pursuing all available debt collection remedies simultaneously, provided that collections do not exceed the amount of the debt, including any interest, penalties, and administrative costs.

claims.quote: The term “centralized offset” includes the Treasury Offset Program's processing of offsets of Federal payments disbursed by disbursing officials other than Fiscal Service.
claims.summary: The Treasury Offset Program must process the offsets of Federal payments disbursed by disbursing officials other than Fiscal Service.

claims.quote: The term “debt” does not include debts arising under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (26 U.S.C. 1 et seq. ), the tariff laws of the United States, or the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 301 et seq. ), except to the extent provided in sections 204(f) and 1631(b)(4) of such Act (42 U.S.C. 404(f) and 1383(b)(4)(A), respectively) and 31 U.S.C. 3716(c).
claims.summary: The term 'debt' does not include debts arising under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, the tariff laws of the United States, or the Social Security Act, except to the extent provided in sections 204(f) and 1631(b)(4) of such Act and 31 U.S.C. 3716(c).

claims.quote: (1) Creditor agencies shall submit delinquent debts to Fiscal Service for purposes of offset in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must submit delinquent debts to Fiscal Service for purposes of offset.

claims.quote: (2) Disbursing officials shall compare payment records with delinquent debt records submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by offset. When a match occurs, and all other requirements for offset have been met, the disbursing official shall offset the payment to satisfy, in whole or part, the payee's debt to the extent allowed by law. The disbursing official shall pay any amounts not offset to the payee.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must compare payment records with delinquent debt records and offset payments to satisfy the payee's debt when all requirements are met.

claims.quote: (1) Mandatory notification of delinquent debts. As required by 31 U.S.C. 3716(c)(6), and in accordance with the provisions of this section, a creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service of all legally enforceable debts over 120 days delinquent that are owed to the creditor agency.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must notify Fiscal Service of all legally enforceable debts over 120 days delinquent.

claims.quote: (ii) The creditor agency must certify that the debt is eligible for collection by offset, as required in paragraph (d)(6) of this section.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must certify that the debt is eligible for collection by offset.

claims.quote: (iv) In accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3719 and the procedures promulgated thereunder, creditor agencies must report to Treasury the amount of debt over 120 days delinquent eligible for the Treasury Offset Program. The procedures require that such report include the amount of debt over 120 days delinquent that the creditor agency has determined is not eligible for the Treasury Offset Program and the reasons for such determination.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must report to Treasury the amount of debt over 120 days delinquent eligible for the Treasury Offset Program, including the amount not eligible and the reasons.

claims.quote: (4) Creditor agency regulations. Prior to submitting a debt to Fiscal Service for purposes of offset, Federal agencies shall prescribe regulations in accordance with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716(b), 31 CFR 901.3(b)(4), 31 U.S.C. 3720A(a), and 31 CFR 285.2(c). Before submitting debts to Fiscal Service for purposes of offsetting Federal salary payments, creditor agencies must also publish regulations pursuant to 5 U.S.C.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must prescribe regulations in accordance with specified requirements before submitting a debt to Fiscal Service for purposes of offset.

claims.quote: (5) Delinquent debt information requirements. For each debt submitted to Fiscal Service for offset, the creditor agency shall provide the following information: (i) Name and taxpayer identifying number of the person who owes the debt; (ii) Debtor's address last known to the creditor agency; (iii) The amount of the debt (including, as applicable, interest, penalties and administrative costs) and the date on which the debt became delinquent; (iv) The address and telephone number of the contact point within the creditor agency who will handle questions, concerns or communications regarding the debt; (v) Written certification as required in paragraph (d)(6) of this section; and (vi) Other information as may be requested by Fiscal Service.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must provide specific information about each debt submitted to Fiscal Service for offset, including the debtor's details, debt amount, contact information, and written certification.

claims.quote: (6) Creditor agency certification. At the time the creditor agency notifies Fiscal Service of a debt for purposes of collection by offset, the creditor agency shall provide, in the manner required by Fiscal Service, written certification to Fiscal Service that: (i) The debt meets the requirements described in paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section; (ii) In compliance with 31 U.S.C. 3, 3720A, 26 U.S.C. 6402, and applicable regulations, the creditor agency has made a reasonable attempt to provide each debtor with: (A) Written notification, at least sixty days prior to submitting the debt and at the debtor's most current address known to the agency, of the nature and the amount of the debt, the intention of the creditor agency to collect the debt through offset, and an explanation of the rights of the debtor; (B) An opportunity to inspect and copy the records of the creditor agency with respect to the debt; (C) An opportunity for a review within the creditor agency of the determination of indebtedness, including the opportunity to present evidence that all or part of the debt is not past-due or legally enforceable; (D) An opportunity to enter into a written repayment agreement with the creditor agency; and (E) In the case of Federal employees, an opportunity for a hearing prior to submitting the debt for Federal salary offset.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must provide written certification to Fiscal Service that the debt meets specific requirements, including providing the debtor with notification, access to records, review opportunities, repayment agreements, and hearings for Federal employees.

claims.quote: (iii) For debts outstanding more than ten years on or before June 11, 2009, the notice of intent to offset described in paragraph (d)(6)(ii)(A) of this section was sent to the debtor after the debt was outstanding for more than ten years, and that the debtor was afforded the rights described in paragraphs (d)(6)(ii)(B) through (E). This requirement will apply even in a case where notice was also sent prior to the debt being outstanding for ten years but does not apply to any debt that could be collected by offset without regard to any time limitation prior to June 11, 2009.
claims.summary: For debts outstanding more than ten years on or before June 11, 2009, the creditor agency must ensure that the notice of intent to offset was sent after the debt was outstanding for more than ten years and that the debtor was afforded the rights described in paragraphs (d)(6)(ii)(B) through (E).

claims.quote: (iv) The creditor agency has complied with all statutes, regulations, and policies applicable to the creditor agency's assessment of interest, penalties and administrative costs (including, as applicable, 31 U.S.C. 3717), and that the creditor agency has provided a written notice to debtors explaining the creditor agency's requirements concerning any such charges assessed against those debtors;
claims.summary: The creditor agency must certify that it has complied with all applicable statutes, regulations, and policies regarding the assessment of interest, penalties, and administrative costs, and that it has provided written notice to debtors about these requirements.

claims.quote: (v) The individual signing the certification has the delegated authority to execute the certification on behalf of the head of the creditor agency; and
claims.summary: The individual signing the certification must have the delegated authority to execute it on behalf of the head of the creditor agency.

claims.quote: (vi) Such additional information that Fiscal Service may from time to time require in compliance with law, regulation or policy.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must provide any additional information that Fiscal Service may require in compliance with law, regulation, or policy.

claims.quote: (7) Updating certification.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must update the certification as required.

claims.quote: the creditor agency shall provide, at least annually, in the manner and time frames required by Fiscal Service, written certification to Fiscal Service that: (i) The debt continues to meet the requirements described in paragraph (d)(3) of this section; and (ii) The creditor agency has properly credited all collections to the debt balance (other than collections received through centralized offset).
claims.summary: The creditor agency must provide annual written certification to Fiscal Service that the debt meets requirements and that all collections have been properly credited.

claims.quote: Agencies will provide the certification in a form and manner prescribed by Fiscal Service. Fiscal Service will instruct agencies as to the form such written certifications will take and how certifications can be delivered to Fiscal Service, including, but not limited to, the use of electronic data transmission.
claims.summary: Agencies must provide certification in a form and manner prescribed by Fiscal Service, and Fiscal Service will instruct on the form and delivery method.

claims.quote: the creditor agency must properly credit all collections, other than collections received from centralized offset.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must properly credit all collections, excluding those received from centralized offset.

claims.quote: The creditor agency shall update delinquent debt records, in the manner and time frames required by Fiscal Service, to reflect any amounts credited by the creditor agency to the debtor's account after submission of the debt to Fiscal Service (other than credits for amounts collected by centralized offset).
claims.summary: The creditor agency must update delinquent debt records to reflect amounts credited to the debtor's account after submission, excluding credits from centralized offset.

claims.quote: The creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service immediately of any change in the status of the legal enforceability of the debt—for example, if the creditor agency receives notice that the debtor has filed for bankruptcy protection.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must notify Fiscal Service immediately of any change in the legal enforceability status of the debt.

claims.quote: The creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service if it has returned any monies to the debtor/payee.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must notify Fiscal Service if it has returned any monies to the debtor/payee.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service, the debt collection center, or the Department of Justice, as the case may be, is responsible for submitting the debt information to Fiscal Service to satisfy the creditor agency's obligations under 31 U.S.C. 3716(c)(6) and this section.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service, the debt collection center, or the Department of Justice is responsible for submitting debt information to satisfy the creditor agency's obligations.

claims.quote: If the creditor agency certifies to Fiscal Service that the creditor agency has determined the offset amount allowed by law would result in financial hardship to the debtor and that a lesser offset amount (specified either in dollar amount or as a percentage of the payment) is reasonable and appropriate based on the debtor's financial circumstances, then the disbursing official shall offset such lesser amount specified by the creditor agency.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must certify to Fiscal Service that a lesser offset amount is reasonable and appropriate based on the debtor's financial circumstances.

claims.quote: Except as set forth in paragraph (e)(2) of this section, all Federal payments are eligible for offset under this section.
claims.summary: Federal payments are eligible for offset unless specified otherwise.

claims.quote: Eligible Federal payments include, but are not limited to, Federal wage, salary, and retirement payments, vendor and expense reimbursement payments, certain benefit payments, travel advances and reimbursements, grants, fees, refunds, judgments (including those certified for payment pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 1304), tax refunds, and other payments made by Federal agencies.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must include specific types of payments in eligible offset categories.

claims.quote: This section does not apply to the following payments: (i) Black Lung Part C benefit payments, or Railroad Retirement tier 2 payments; (ii) Payments made under the tariff laws of the United States; (iii) Veterans Affairs benefit payments to the extent such payments are exempt from offset pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 5301; (iv) Payments made under any program administered by the Secretary of Education under title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965 for which payments are certified by the Department of Education; (v) Payments made under any other Federal law if offset is expressly prohibited by Federal statute; (vi) Payments made under any program for which the Secretary has granted an exemption in accordance with the provisions of 31 U.S.C. 3716(c)(3)(B) and paragraph (e)(7) of this section; and (vii) Federal loan payments other than travel advances.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must exclude specific payments from offset under this section.

claims.quote: If a payment is certified to more than one payee (i.e., joint payees), the entire payment (including a tax refund payment) will be subject to offset for a debt of either payee, unless otherwise prohibited by law or regulation.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must subject payments to joint payees to offset for a debt of either payee.

claims.quote: If a payment is made to a person solely in that person's capacity as a representative payee for another person having the beneficial interest in a payment, the disbursing official shall offset that payment only to collect debts owed by the person having the beneficial interest in the payment.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must offset payments made to representative payees only for debts owed by the person with beneficial interest.

claims.quote: If a person, including a Federal contractor, assigns the right to receive a Federal payment to a third party (the “assignee”), the assigned payment will be subject to offset to collect a delinquent debt owed by the assignee.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must subject assigned payments to offset for delinquent debts owed by the assignee.

claims.quote: An assigned payment will also be subject to offset to collect delinquent debts owed by the assignor unless: (A) In accordance with 41 U.S.C. 15(e)-(f), the payment has been properly assigned to a financial institution pursuant to a Federal contract, the contract contains provisions prohibiting the payment from being reduced or offset for debts owed by the contractor, and the debt arose independently of the contract; or (B) pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3727, the payment is being made to the assignee as settlement or satisfaction of a claim brought by the assignee against the creditor agency based upon the contract, and the debt of the contractor arises independently of the contract; or (C) the debtor has properly assigned the right to such payments and the debt arose after the effective date of the assignment.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must subject assigned payments to offset for delinquent debts owed by the assignor unless specific exceptions apply.

claims.quote: The Secretary will exempt from centralized offset payments made under means-tested programs when requested by the head of the agency making such payments.
claims.summary: The Secretary must exempt payments made under means-tested programs when requested by the head of the agency making such payments.

claims.quote: The Secretary may exempt classes of payments which are not means-tested. Payment agencies may request that the Secretary exempt 100% of each payment in a payment class or that the Secretary exempt a specific lesser percentage.
claims.summary: Payment agencies may request the Secretary to exempt classes of non-means-tested payments, either 100% of each payment or a specific lesser percentage.

claims.quote: The head of the payment agency must make a request for exemption in writing.
claims.summary: The head of the payment agency must make a written request for exemption.

claims.quote: The request must comply with the procedures published by Fiscal Service and made available at its Web site.
claims.summary: The request must comply with the procedures published by Fiscal Service and made available at its Web site.

claims.quote: The Secretary will only exempt classes of payments. Requests for exemption of individual payments will not be considered.
claims.summary: The Secretary will only exempt classes of payments. Requests for exemption of individual payments will not be considered.

claims.quote: Payment agencies shall prepare and submit payment vouchers in the manner prescribed by the disbursing official to ensure that all payments legally eligible for offset will be offset and all payments not eligible will not be offset.
claims.summary: Payment agencies must prepare and submit payment vouchers in the manner prescribed by the disbursing official to ensure that all payments legally eligible for offset will be offset and all payments not eligible will not be offset.

claims.quote: Payment agencies shall also review the nature of payments the agency certifies and notify Fiscal Service of any legal bars to centralized offset of payments.
claims.summary: Payment agencies must review the nature of payments they certify and notify Fiscal Service of any legal bars to centralized offset of payments.

claims.quote: When an offset occurs, the debtor has received payment in full for the underlying obligation represented by the payment. Pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(c)(2)(A), neither the disbursing official nor the payment agency shall be liable for the amount of the offset on the basis that the underlying obligation was not satisfied.
claims.summary: When an offset occurs, the debtor has received payment in full for the underlying obligation. Neither the disbursing official nor the payment agency shall be liable for the amount of the offset on the basis that the underlying obligation was not satisfied.

claims.quote: The disbursing official shall offset the payee's Federal payment to satisfy, in whole or part, the debt owed by the debtor.
claims.summary: The disbursing official must offset the payee's Federal payment to satisfy, in whole or part, the debt owed by the debtor.

claims.quote: Offsets will continue until the debt, including any interest, penalties, and administrative costs, is paid in full or otherwise resolved to the satisfaction of the creditor agency.
claims.summary: Offsets will continue until the debt, including any interest, penalties, and administrative costs, is paid in full or otherwise resolved to the satisfaction of the creditor agency.

claims.quote: Except as otherwise provided in 31 CFR 285.4(e) and 285.7(g), the disbursing official shall offset the lesser of: (A) The amount of the payment as shown on the payment record; or (B) The amount of the debt, including any interest, penalties and administrative costs; or (C) In the case of retirement annuity payments certified by the Office of Personnel Management, up to twenty-five percent of the amount of the payment as shown on the payment record.
claims.summary: The disbursing official must offset the lesser of the amount of the payment as shown on the payment record, the amount of the debt, or up to twenty-five percent of the payment in the case of retirement annuity payments.

claims.quote: the disbursing official shall offset the amount specified by the creditor agency.
claims.summary: The disbursing official must offset the amount specified by the creditor agency.

claims.quote: the disbursing official, or Fiscal Service on behalf of the disbursing official, will notify the payee in writing when offsets will begin...
claims.summary: The disbursing official must notify the payee in writing when offsets will begin.

claims.quote: the disbursing official, or Fiscal Service on behalf of the disbursing official, shall notify the payee in writing that an offset has occurred including...
claims.summary: The disbursing official must notify the payee in writing that an offset has occurred.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will notify the creditor agency of all offsets made to collect the creditor agency's debts.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must notify the creditor agency of all offsets made to collect the creditor agency's debts.

claims.quote: When a non-Treasury disbursing official conducts the offset, that disbursing official will transmit to Fiscal Service all of the information necessary for Fiscal Service to send notification...
claims.summary: A non-Treasury disbursing official must transmit all necessary information to Fiscal Service for notification.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will make available to the payment agency the information contained in the notification of offset...
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must make available to the payment agency the information from the offset notification.

claims.quote: (1) Fiscal Service will transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged pursuant to paragraph (j) of this section, to the appropriate creditor agency or agencies. Alternatively, Fiscal Service may bill the creditor agency for any fees charged pursuant to paragraph (j) of this section.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees, to the appropriate creditor agency or agencies. Alternatively, Fiscal Service may bill the creditor agency for any fees.

claims.quote: (2) If Fiscal Service learns from a paying agency that a payment should not have been made, and thus not offset, Fiscal Service will notify the creditor agency. Fiscal Service may deduct the offset amount from future amounts payable to the creditor agency. Alternatively, upon Fiscal Service's request, the creditor agency shall return promptly to the disbursing official an amount equal to the amount of the offset (without regard to whether any other amounts payable to such disbursing official have been paid).
claims.summary: If Fiscal Service learns a payment should not have been made, it must notify the creditor agency. Fiscal Service may deduct the offset amount from future payments. Alternatively, upon request, the creditor agency must return the offset amount to the disbursing official.

claims.quote: (3) Generally, the disbursing official is not responsible for refunding money to debtors. The creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service any time the creditor agency returns all or any part of an offset payment to an affected payee. See paragraph (d)(10)(v) of this section. Fiscal Service and the creditor agency shall adjust the debtor records appropriately.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must notify Fiscal Service whenever it returns all or part of an offset payment to an affected payee. Fiscal Service and the creditor agency must adjust debtor records accordingly.

claims.quote: (j) Fees. Fiscal Service may charge a fee sufficient to cover the full cost of implementing the centralized offset program, including the amount of any fees charged by other disbursing officials conducting an offset under this section. Fiscal Service may deduct the fees from amounts collected by offset or may bill the creditor agencies. Fiscal Service will charge fees only for actual offsets collected.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may charge fees to cover the full cost of implementing the centralized offset program. Fees may be deducted from collected amounts or billed to creditor agencies. Fees are only charged for actual offsets collected.

claims.quote: (l) Social Security numbers. Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail. In addition, Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer the Treasury Offset Program, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must ensure Social Security numbers are not visible on the outside of mailed packages. It generally must redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents. However, it may include them in mailed documents for specific purposes such as interoffice communications, notices about offsets, responses to debtor requests, or when required by law.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service and other disbursing officials of the Federal Government will conduct administrative offset to collect past-due State debts certified to Fiscal Service, and participating States will conduct State payment offset to collect delinquent Federal debts in accordance with the terms of reciprocal agreements entered into between the States and Fiscal Service, acting on behalf of the Secretary.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service and participating States must conduct administrative offset and State payment offset, respectively, to collect delinquent debts in accordance with reciprocal agreements.

claims.quote: Upon notification of a delinquent State debt from a participating State to Fiscal Service, disbursing officials of the United States shall offset the Federal payments specified in the reciprocal agreement to collect the State debt.
claims.affected_party: disbursing officials of the United States
claims.summary: Disbursing officials of the United States must offset Federal payments specified in the reciprocal agreement to collect delinquent State debts.

claims.quote: The amount offset, minus an offset fee, shall be forwarded to the State to be distributed in accordance with applicable laws and procedures.
claims.affected_party: disbursing officials of the United States
claims.summary: The amount offset, minus an offset fee, must be forwarded to the State to be distributed in accordance with applicable laws and procedures.

claims.quote: Upon notification of a delinquent Federal debt from Fiscal Service to a participating State, authorized officials of the participating State shall conduct State payment offset as specified in the applicable reciprocal agreement to collect the Federal debt.
claims.affected_party: authorized officials of the participating State
claims.summary: Authorized officials of the participating State must conduct State payment offset as specified in the applicable reciprocal agreement to collect delinquent Federal debts.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may enter into reciprocal agreements with States for administrative offset and State payment offset. The agreements shall contain any requirements which Fiscal Service considers appropriate to facilitate the offset and prevent duplicative efforts, and shall require States to prescribe procedures governing the collection of delinquent State debts which are substantially similar to requirements imposed on Federal agencies pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(b).
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may enter into reciprocal agreements with States for administrative offset and State payment offset, which must contain requirements to facilitate the offset and prevent duplicative efforts, and require States to prescribe procedures substantially similar to those imposed on Federal agencies.

claims.quote: States may prescribe such procedures through legislation or regulations, as deemed appropriate by State officials.
claims.summary: States may prescribe procedures through legislation or regulations, as deemed appropriate by State officials.

claims.quote: States which have entered into a reciprocal agreement with Fiscal Service pursuant to this section may thereafter request, in the manner prescribed in the reciprocal agreement, that administrative offsets be performed. Such requests shall be made by the appropriate State disbursing official, which, for purposes of this section, means an appropriate official of the State agency that is responsible for collecting the State debt.
claims.summary: States that have entered into a reciprocal agreement with Fiscal Service may request administrative offsets to be performed in the manner prescribed in the reciprocal agreement, with such requests made by the appropriate State disbursing official.

claims.quote: Reciprocal agreements must be signed by a State official authorized to enter into such agreements.
claims.summary: Reciprocal agreements must be signed by a State official authorized to enter into such agreements.

claims.quote: Once Fiscal Service has entered into a reciprocal agreement with a State pursuant to this section, Fiscal Service may request that the State perform State payment offsets to collect delinquent Federal debts in accordance with the terms of the reciprocal agreement.
claims.summary: Once Fiscal Service has entered into a reciprocal agreement with a State, Fiscal Service may request that the State perform State payment offsets to collect delinquent Federal debts in accordance with the terms of the reciprocal agreement.

claims.quote: A duly executed reciprocal agreement is required before a State may request an administrative offset pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(h).
claims.summary: A duly executed reciprocal agreement is required before a State may request an administrative offset pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(h).

claims.quote: A State debt submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset must meet the debt eligibility requirements of 31 CFR 285.5(d)(3)(i).
claims.summary: A State debt submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset must meet the debt eligibility requirements of 31 CFR 285.5(d)(3)(i).

claims.quote: At the time a participating State notifies Fiscal Service of a State debt for purposes of collection by administrative offset under this section, the State shall comply with the certification requirements set forth in paragraph 31 CFR 285.5(d)(6) with the following two exceptions: (i) Paragraph (d)(6)(ii)(E)—Federal salary offset; and (ii) Paragraph (d)(6)(iii)—Federal requirements for the assessment of interest and penalties to Federal debts.
claims.summary: At the time a participating State notifies Fiscal Service of a State debt for purposes of collection by administrative offset, the State shall comply with the certification requirements set forth in paragraph 31 CFR 285.5(d)(6), with the exceptions of Federal salary offset and Federal requirements for the assessment of interest and penalties to Federal debts.

claims.quote: Additionally, with respect to paragraph (d)(6)(ii) of § 285.5, States shall only be required to certify that they have complied with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716 (not 31 U.S.C. 3720A or 26 U.S.C. 6402) and this section 285.6. States shall also certify that they have complied with any requirements imposed by State law or procedure that may be applicable to administrative offset.
claims.summary: With respect to paragraph (d)(6)(ii) of § 285.5, States shall only be required to certify that they have complied with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716 and this section 285.6, and also certify that they have complied with any requirements imposed by State law or procedure that may be applicable to administrative offset.

claims.quote: A State shall be deemed to have complied with the requirements of paragraph (e)(2) of this section with respect to any State debt that the State certified to Treasury for collection pursuant to
claims.summary: A State shall be deemed to have complied with the requirements of paragraph (e)(2) of this section with respect to any State debt that the State certified to Treasury for collection pursuant to.

claims.quote: The Federal payments that will be offset to collect a participating State's debts shall be set forth in the reciprocal agreement.
claims.summary: The Federal payments subject to offset must be set forth in the reciprocal agreement.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials shall conduct administrative offset under this section in the same manner as set forth in 31 CFR 285.5(f) through (i).
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must conduct administrative offset in the same manner as set forth in 31 CFR 285.5(f) through (i).

claims.quote: Neither the Federal disbursing official nor the agency authorizing the Federal payment shall be liable to a debtor for the amount of the administrative offset on the basis that the underlying obligation, represented by the payment before the administrative offset was taken, was not satisfied.
claims.affected_party: Federal disbursing official and agency authorizing the Federal payment
claims.summary: The Federal disbursing official and the agency authorizing the Federal payment shall not be liable to a debtor for the amount of the administrative offset if the underlying obligation was not satisfied.

claims.quote: A State may set forth in the reciprocal agreement the requirements for Fiscal Service to follow when submitting a Federal debt for collection by State payment offset. Such agreements shall set forth all requirements contained in State law for the State payment offset.
claims.summary: A State may set forth in the reciprocal agreement the requirements for Fiscal Service to follow when submitting a Federal debt for collection by State payment offset, including all requirements contained in State law for the State payment offset.

claims.quote: (2) Fiscal Service shall certify to a participating State that each debt Fiscal Service submits for State payment offset has been certified by the Federal creditor agency to be delinquent, valid, and legally enforceable in the amount stated, and that the Federal creditor agency owed the debt has complied with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716(a) prior to submitting the debt for offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must certify to a participating State that each debt submitted for State payment offset is delinquent, valid, and legally enforceable, and that the Federal creditor agency has complied with 31 U.S.C. 3716(a).

claims.quote: (1) An official of a participating State shall conduct State payment offset pursuant to the laws and regulations of the participating State; provided that: (i) If a payment is owed jointly to more than one payee, the entire payment shall be offset for a debt of either payee, unless otherwise prohibited by law or regulation; and (ii) If a payment is made to a person solely in that person's capacity as a representative payee for another person having the beneficial interest in the payment, the disbursing official shall offset that payment only to collect debts owed by the person having the beneficial interest in the payment.
claims.affected_party: An official of a participating State
claims.summary: An official of a participating State must conduct State payment offset according to the laws and regulations of the participating State, with specific provisions for joint payments and representative payees.

claims.quote: (3) An official of the participating State shall notify the payee of the State payment offset. The reciprocal agreement may contain detailed guidance and procedures regarding sending such notice, but shall, at a minimum require that the notice inform the payee of: (i) The type and amount of the payment that was offset; (ii) The identity of the Federal agency that requested the offset; and (iii) A contact point within the Federal agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.affected_party: An official of the participating State
claims.summary: An official of the participating State must notify the payee of the State payment offset, with the notice requiring to inform the payee of the type and amount of the payment offset, the identity of the Federal agency that requested the offset, and a contact point within the Federal agency.

claims.quote: (l) Limitations. A debt properly submitted to Fiscal Service or the State for administrative offset or State payment offset shall remain subject to collection until withdrawn by the entity that submitted the debt for collection, provided the debt remains past-due and legally enforceable for purposes of administrative offset or State payment offset, as applicable. A debt which has been reduced to a judgment shall remain legally enforceable for purposes of administrative offset and State payment offset for as long as the judgment remains enforceable against the debtor.
claims.affected_party: Entity that submitted the debt for collection
claims.summary: A debt properly submitted for administrative offset or State payment offset remains subject to collection until withdrawn by the entity that submitted the debt, provided the debt remains past-due and legally enforceable. A debt reduced to a judgment remains legally enforceable for as long as the judgment is enforceable against the debtor.

claims.quote: (m) Fees. Fiscal Service shall deduct a fee from each administrative offset and State payment offset amount before transferring the balance of the offset funds to the State or Federal agency owed the debt. Pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(c)(4), the fee will be in an amount that Fiscal Service has determined to be sufficient to reimburse Fiscal Service for the full cost of the offset procedure. Fiscal Service will notify the States and creditor agencies, annually and in advance, of the amount of the fee Fiscal Service will charge for each offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must deduct a fee from each administrative offset and State payment offset amount before transferring the balance of the offset funds to the State or Federal agency owed the debt. Fiscal Service must notify the States and creditor agencies annually and in advance of the fee amount.

claims.quote: (n) Social Security numbers. Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail. In addition, Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer administrative offset, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must ensure that an individual's Social Security number is not visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail and generally redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents sent by mail. However, Fiscal Service may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents for specific purposes such as interoffice communications, notices about offsets, responses to requests for records, and when required by law.

claims.quote: This section implements the requirement under 5 U.S.C. 5514(a)(1) that all Federal agencies, using a process known as centralized salary offset computer matching, identify Federal employees who owe delinquent nontax debt to the United States.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must identify Federal employees who owe delinquent nontax debt to the United States using centralized salary offset computer matching.

claims.quote: This section specifies the delinquent debt records and Federal employee records that must be included in the salary offset matching process.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must include delinquent debt records and Federal employee records in the salary offset matching process.

claims.quote: This section establishes an interagency consortium to implement centralized salary offset computer matching on a government-wide basis as required under 5 U.S.C. 5514(a)(1).
claims.summary: Federal agencies must participate in an interagency consortium to implement centralized salary offset computer matching on a government-wide basis.

claims.quote: Agencies that submit their debt to Fiscal Service for purposes of administrative offset are not required to submit duplicate information for purposes of centralized salary offset computer matching under 5 U.S.C. 5514 and this section.
claims.summary: Federal agencies that submit their debt to Fiscal Service for administrative offset are not required to submit duplicate information for centralized salary offset computer matching.
